captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus #1 2x pick across all channels. Topped FP2, expected to qualify front row and fight for the win. Has taken fastest lap in 6 of 9 races. Estimated 30-35 points. Safest and highest-floor option.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Isaac Hajar
captains.reason: Starting P21/P22 due to engine penalty. Could gain 12-14 positions with massive overtake points (24+ from position gains alone). Driver of the day candidate. Multiple channels note Autopilot chip viability on Hajar as he could challenge Antonelli's total. ZachGP calls him a viable Autopilot 2x pick.

buy.name: Isaac Hajar
buy.note: Must-have across all channels. Back-of-grid penalty with top-10 expected finish (betting lines say P8). Five straight top-6 finishes. Needs only -2 points for min price rise. Massive overtake/position-gain upside.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Universal must-have. Needs only 1 point for max price rise of 0.6M. Racing Bulls looked strong in top 10 across FP1/FP2. Best points-per-million asset available.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Popular Hulkenberg replacement. P10 in FP1. Needs 3 points for max price rise. Audi brought Spa-spec rear wing. Multiple channels prefer him over Hulkenberg for cost cap upside.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Consistent midfield scorer, needs 6 points for max rise which is easily attainable. V-Carb entrenched in top 10 in FP sessions. Slight discount to Colapinto with similar upside.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Best price-rise thresholds (-8 for min, 1 point for max 0.6M rise). Quicker Alpine on Friday. But Alpine languished P15 in FP1; some channels prefer Lawson at a discount. FanAmp notes sacrificing one max price increase for Hajar's points is worthwhile.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: One of only two drivers (with Hamilton) to score 7+ points every race. 6.4 overtakes per race. Needs only 2 points for min rise. Consolation if 0.1M short of Colapinto.

consider.name: Nico Hulkenberg
consider.note: Floor price, cannot drop. Audi brought Spa rear wing so should compete around top 10. Multiple channels are moving off him to Bortoleto but he remains viable for lowest-budget builds.

consider.name: Lando Norris
consider.note: 10-place grid penalty. FanAmp ran the numbers: best case ~30 pts on Sunday vs Antonelli's typical 35. Betting lines predict P7 finish. Consensus is he's NOT worth 2x boost or Final Fix chip. Nice to have alongside Antonelli but not as primary captain.

avoid: Lance Stroll — P22 regardless of penalty, not a points source; wait for Aston Martin Hungary upgrades
Fernando Alonso — said his goal Sunday is to get home to watch Spain in the World Cup final; wait for Hungary upgrades
Sergio Perez — no channel mentions him as viable
Pierre Gasly — heavy FP2 crash, 13M price too high vs Hajar at similar cost
Carlos Sainz — not mentioned as viable by any channel
Alex Albon — fighting to escape Q1, not viable

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: Multiple channels highlight this as the best Autopilot weekend of the season. Hajar starting P21/P22 could outscore Antonelli on race day, making the chip valuable if you believe Hajar's race points exceed Antonelli's total. FormulaFantasyHub and F1FantasyPolePosition both seriously considering it. ZachGP notes Hajar is a viable Autopilot play. Use only if you genuinely believe Hajar will be the weekend's top scorer.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Strong consensus to save. FanAmp ran detailed numbers: Norris's best-case Sunday (~30 pts) doesn't beat a typical Antonelli Sunday (~35 pts). ZachGP acknowledges it's a 'nice option' but recommends holding. F1FantasyPolePosition calls Final Fix a 'break glass in case of emergency' chip worth preserving.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: FanAmp notes No Negative is 'always in play at Spa' due to the circuit's history of incidents and DNFs. Worth considering if you have high-risk assets, but not explicitly recommended over Autopilot this week.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No channel recommends using Wildcard this week. Hungary with Aston Martin upgrades may be a better deployment.

Red Bull removed the 'Macarena wing' that reportedly caused Verstappen's recent retirements — Max topped FP1 and looked strong, boosting Red Bull constructor case
Exact Hajar penalty position (P21 vs P22) depends on penalty stacking with Stroll — affects overtake ceiling
Weather: increasing cloudiness, 25% rain chance Sunday — Spa microclimate could scramble the grid
arc: Belgium sets up a critical transition into Hungary. Aston Martin are bringing upgrades to the Hungaroring, potentially making Alonso and Stroll viable budget assets for the first time. Teams should prioritize budget building this week through Lindblad, Colapinto, and Bortoleto price rises while capturing Hajar's massive one-off scoring opportunity. The Red Bull constructor case strengthens if Verstappen maintains front-row form and Hajar delivers from the back. Hungary is a tighter, Monaco-style circuit where overtaking is harder, so the grid-penalty bonanza at Spa is a unique opportunity — capture the points now and pivot to a more qualifying-focused strategy for the Hungaroring. Hold Final Fix and Wildcard chips for future deployment when the value equation is clearer.
